item.text:
## 1B.4: Arms control / disarmament / de-escalation in 2023

**Working judgment:** **Mostly no.** Putin’s 2023 record contains one formal pro-arms-control declaration, but the year’s clearest concrete move was suspending New START participation and using nuclear signaling as leverage. I found no credible 2023 evidence of good-faith progress on inspections, disarmament, or de-escalation agreements.

### Accepted claims

- **Title:** `Указ Президента Российской Федерации от 31.03.2023 г. № 229`  
  **Publisher:** Kremlin  
  **Date:** 31 Mar 2023  
  **URL:** [https://www.kremlin.ru/acts/bank/49090/print](https://www.kremlin.ru/acts/bank/49090/print)  
  **Claim-level summary:** Russia’s updated foreign-policy concept says it will support strategic stability, arms control, nonproliferation, prevention of nuclear and WMD risks, and phased reductions in nuclear potential. This is the strongest 2023 pro-1B.4 evidence, but it is declaratory policy rather than a verified negotiating outcome or inspection commitment actually pursued in good faith.  
  **Question IDs:** `1B.4`, `1B.1`, `1B.3`

- **Title:** `Russia's Putin issues new nuclear warnings to West over Ukraine`  
  **Publisher:** Reuters  
  **Date:** 21 Feb 2023  
  **URL:** [https://gulfnews.com/world/europe/russias-putin-issues-new-nuclear-warnings-to-west-over-ukraine-1.1676971364764](https://gulfnews.com/world/europe/russias-putin-issues-new-nuclear-warnings-to-west-over-ukraine-1.1676971364764)  
  **Claim-level summary:** In Putin’s 21 February 2023 address, he announced suspension of Russia’s participation in New START, said new strategic systems had been put on combat duty, and threatened to resume nuclear testing. That is strong evidence **against** good-faith support for arms control or de-escalation.  
  **Question IDs:** `1B.4`, `1B.1`, `1B.2`

- **Title:** `Russia Suspends New START`  
  **Publisher:** Arms Control Association  
  **Date:** March 2023  
  **URL:** [https://www.armscontrol.org/act/2023-03/news/russia-suspends-new-start](https://www.armscontrol.org/act/2023-03/news/russia-suspends-new-start)  
  **Claim-level summary:** This account says Putin announced suspension of New START and tied any resumption to U.S. concessions on Ukraine and broader arms-control talks. That conditional linkage is inconsistent with good-faith treaty support and reinforces the negative reading.  
  **Question IDs:** `1B.4`, `1B.1`

### Search gap

I did **not** find reliable 2023 evidence of Putin taking concrete good-faith steps such as restoring inspections, agreeing to verifiable limits, entering new disarmament arrangements, or lowering nuclear tensions through sustained treaty implementation. The pro-arms-control language in March 2023 was outweighed by the February suspension of New START and the coercive framing around it.

### Bottom line

**Mostly no.** The year shows formal pro-arms-control wording, but the actionable record points the other way: suspension of a major arms-control treaty and nuclear brinkmanship rather than good-faith support for de-escalation agreements.
